# waveoptics.py
*`src/pySEA/rayTEM/waveoptics.py`*

Paraxial scalar wave-optics primitives for rayTEM.

### `kernel_phase(shape, dx, dy, wavelength, dz, include_carrier=True)`
Reciprocal-space free-segment phase χ = k·dz − π·λ·dz·(f_x²+f_y²) on the
unshifted `fftfreq` grid. `include_carrier=False` drops the k·dz carrier — the
scaled path (Eq 32) uses that form.

### `apply_phase(field, phase, space='position')`
The single phase-application primitive: `space='position'` multiplies by
exp(iχ) in real space; `space='scattering'` applies exp(iχ) in the FFT domain.
Consumes the space tag carried by `phase_shift` items (`seashells.phase_space_of`).

### `quadratic_phase(shape, dx, dy, wavelength, power_x, power_y)`
Phase-*returning* lens builder: χ = −k(P_x·x² + P_y·y²)/2. A quadrupole is the
astigmatic case P_x = −P_y.

### `linear_phase(shape, dx, dy, wavelength, tilt_x, tilt_y)`
Phase-*returning* tilt builder: χ = k(θ_x·x + θ_y·y).

### `angular_spectrum_propagate(field, dx, dy, wavelength, dz, include_carrier=True)`
Propagate a scalar field a distance ``dz`` in free space (paraxial). Now a thin
wrapper over `kernel_phase` + `apply_phase`; the scaled path reuses it over Δτ
with `include_carrier=False`.

### `focal_phase(field, dx, dy, wavelength, power_x, power_y)`
Apply a (possibly astigmatic) thin focusing phase — thin exp(iχ) wrapper over
`quadratic_phase` (behavior unchanged).

### `tilt_phase(field, dx, dy, wavelength, tilt_x, tilt_y)`
Apply a linear phase ramp that tilts the wavefront (dipole steering) — thin
wrapper over `linear_phase`.

### `aperture_mask(field, dx, dy, radius, antialias=True)`
Apply the hard circular aperture Θ(a−r). Default **anti-aliased**: edge pixels
carry their area-coverage fraction (1-px linear ramp — the projection of the
sharp mask), so above-Nyquist edge content does not fold back and propagate as
an axis-aligned "gridding" pattern; `antialias=False` restores the point-sampled
binary mask. The scaled path masks U at the scaled radius `radius/|s|`.

### `bandlimited_disk(shape, dx, dy, radius)`
Exactly alias-free sampling of the sharp disk Θ(a−r): synthesized from its
analytic spectrum 2πa²·J1(a·k_r)/(a·k_r) on the discrete frequency grid up to
Nyquist and inverse-FFT'd. Every representable Fresnel fringe is exact and
nothing folds; the band limit shows as Gibbs ripple at the edge (the honest
sampled discontinuity). Used by `Source._aperture_wave` (`wave_kind='aperture'`).

### `boundary_window(shape, margin=0.1)`
Absorbing-boundary window, **radially symmetric** (1 inside the inscribed
circle minus the band, raised-cosine → 0 at the inscribed-circle edge). The
FFT propagator is periodic — field leaving the FOV re-enters and interferes;
physically those electrons leave the beam, so `propagate_free_scaled(absorb>0)`
applies this window between τ sub-steps sized so nothing can cross the band in
one step. Isotropy is a hard requirement: a separable (square) window clips
the halo anisotropically (corners √2 farther than edges) and imprints a
fourfold, pixel-aligned fringe pattern on the beam (measured c4 ~1e-3 at the
basic_column sample/detector; ~0 radial — enforced by a regression test).

## Scaled-Fresnel core (handoff Eqs 23–55)

Pure numerics for `propagate_wave(mode='scaled'|'hybrid')` — the factorization
ψ = (1/s)·U(ξ,η,τ)·exp[ik(x²+y²)/2R], ξ = x/s, 1/R = s′/s, τ = ∫dz/s².
No sea_eco imports (seashells carries the Signal seam; elements orchestrate).

### `scaled_delta_tau(dz, s0, R0)`
Closed-form Δτ = Δz/(s₀²[1 + Δz/R₀]) (Eq 29; Δz/s₀² for R₀ = ∞, Eq 31) —
verified against the numerical ∫dz/s² in the test suite. Raises on an
in-segment s = 0 crossing (Eq 52), naming the crossover position.

### `factor_wave(psi, dx, dy, wavelength, s, R)`
Eq 55: exact factorization of an ordinary wave into (U, Δξ, Δη) for a chosen
frame (s, R). Inverse of `reconstruct_physical_wave`.

### `fourier_resample(field, d_in, n_out, d_out)`
Band-limited resampling by exact separable trigonometric (sinc) interpolation
— two small nonuniform-inverse-DFT matrix products, exact at any pitch ratio.
Used by Eq 44 target-grid reconstruction; value-preserving; grids centered per
`transverse_coordinates`.

### `reconstruct_physical_wave(U, dxi, deta, wavelength, s, R, target_dx=None, target_shape=None)`
Eq 37 (boxed): ψ = (1/s)·U(x/s, y/s)·exp[ik(x²+y²)/2R]. Native grid (Eq 41):
no interpolation, Δx = |s|·Δξ. Prescribed grid (Eq 44): `fourier_resample` of
U at ξ_p = x_p/s. The e^{ikz} carrier is NOT applied.

### `axis_components(value)` / `join_axes(vx, vy)`
The scalar-or-pair convention for **anisotropic frames**
(ψ = (s_x s_y)^{−1/2}·U(x/s_x, y/s_y)·e^{ik(x²/2R_x + y²/2R_y)}): frame
quantities (s, R, τ, powers, z_cross) travel as scalars when the axes agree
and `(x, y)` pairs otherwise. `axis_components` normalizes either form to a
pair; `join_axes` collapses equal components back to a scalar (so round-lens
columns keep scalar state bit-for-bit).

### `apply_thin_lens_scaled(s, R, power)`
Eqs 45–46: 1/R⁺ = 1/R⁻ − power with s continuous; U untouched (Eq 15).
Inf-safe (flat ↔ curved transitions handled). All arguments scalar-or-pair:
a quadrupole's (P, −P) absorbs into (R_x, R_y) exactly like a round lens —
no saddle screen, no sampling limit.

### `beam_support_radius(U, dxi, deta, threshold=1e-6)` / `beam_support_extents(...)`
Per-axis half-widths of the beam's support (largest |ξ|, |η| where
|U| > threshold·max). The sampling criteria measure reference phase at the
**beam**, not the (possibly empty) grid edge — phase applied where the field
is ~0 is harmless — so frames switch at the earliest representable plane for
the actual beam (and padded grids no longer trip the s_min backstop). A beam
filling the grid reproduces the grid-edge criterion exactly.

### `propagate_free_scaled(U, dxi, deta, wavelength, dz, s, R, s_min=1e-3, absorb=0.0)`
One free segment on a single frame: s(z) = s₀[1 + Δz/R₀] (linear),
R(z) = R₀ + Δz, U propagated by the carrier-free angular-spectrum kernel over
Δτ (per-axis Δτ_x/Δτ_y on anisotropic frames — the kernel is separable).
Enforces |s| > s_min on both axes (Eq 52) with an actionable error naming the
crossover — the hybrid engine below switches frames before that ever fires.
`absorb>0` sub-steps in τ and applies `boundary_window` between steps
(removes periodic wraparound; energy honestly decreases by what leaves the FOV).

## Frame switching (crossover traversal)

A **frame** is a factorization choice (s, R, τ) for the same physical wave.
A converging frame is singular at its crossover (s → 0); the wave is not.

### `min_representable_curvature(n, dxi, wavelength, s, safety=0.5, x_max=None)`
|R|_min = k·x_max·Δx/(safety·π): the weakest curvature radius whose reference
phase fits the grid at ≤ safety·π per pixel. Places the flatten/re-diverge
planes and backs the frame-change guard. `x_max` defaults to the grid
half-width; pass `beam_support_radius` to measure at the beam (the engine and
guard both do).

### `change_scaled_frame(U, dxi, deta, wavelength, s_old, R_old, R_new, s_new=None, safety=0.5)`
Eric's Eq 5: re-express the same ψ in another frame — amplitude ratio s_n/s_o
plus the reference-phase difference exp[ik x²/2·(1/R_o − 1/R_n)] — under the
physical-grid-continuous convention (Δξ_n = Δξ_o·s_o/s_n), so the operation is
pointwise. All frame arguments scalar-or-pair (per-axis phase and per-axis
pitch returns; anisotropic amplitude ratio √(s_nx·s_ny/(s_ox·s_oy)), the
isotropic case keeps the signed s_n/s_o bit-for-bit). Guarded per-pixel **at
the beam support**, per axis (the raise names |R|_min and the offending axis);
`safety=None` for the pure converters. `factor_wave` delegates as the
(1, ∞) → (s, R) special case.

### `propagate_free_scaled_hybrid(U, dxi, deta, wavelength, dz, s, R, z, z_cross=None, safety=0.5, s_min=1e-3, absorb=0.0, crossover='flat')`
One free segment with automatic frame switching, all split points in closed
form: a converging frame **flattens** (→ R = ∞, s kept) at |R_flat| = R²/(A·s²)
(a frame invariant; A evaluated at the **beam-support radius** with a 1.2×
spreading margin), crosses the real focus by ordinary carrier-free Fresnel —
the **crossover plane is split out and logged** (the back-focal/diffraction
plane) — and **re-diverges** onto R = +d at d = A·s² past it. Returns the exit
state plus the tagged interior states (`flatten`/`crossover`/`rediverge`);
z_cross is the marker a flat frame carries between elements (rides the scaled
Signal metadata as `z_cross_m`). Internal legs run with the engine's own guard
(closed-form splits; a legitimately deep flatten cannot trip the user s_min).
`crossover='jump'` switches the converging frame directly onto its mirror
diverging frame (R = −d → +d at half the flatten threshold, one switch, no
flat window; tag `jump`) — **measured guidance**: the doubled phase budget
rides 2× deeper, and at tight electron crossovers the focal structure in ξ
(Airy/s) outruns the FOV (the basic_column loses ~95% of its beam), so
`'flat'` is the robust default; use `'jump'` only for mild crossovers.
**Anisotropic frames** run a per-axis event loop (`_hybrid_anisotropic`):
each axis flattens/crosses/re-diverges at its own **line focus** with
axis-suffixed tags (`flatten-x`, `crossover-y`, …) and per-axis z_cross
markers; an isotropic fast path keeps round-lens columns bit-for-bit.
